transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up your time for something silly, but... well, my eating has just gotten a little off lately. It's probably nothing major, you know how it is, but some days I barely get down a coffee and a granola bar before a shift. 

And, um, I've noticed my scrubs have been hanging pretty loose, even though I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything. I just wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by getting it checked out. Is it okay that I came in for that?
Are you avoiding eating because you’re afraid of gaining weight or changing how your body looks?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. Um, I hope I didn't make it sound like that—I really don't want to mislead you. I'm not worried about gaining weight or how my body looks at all. 

It's just... I don't know, I just haven't had much of an appetite, I guess? The thought of eating just hasn't been on my radar as much. I really hope I'm explaining this okay. Does that make sense?
Do you avoid eating because you fear something unpleasant might happen, such as choking, vomiting, or feeling sick?

Oh, no, definitely not that either. I'm sorry, I hope I'm not being difficult by not having a better reason for you. I'm not afraid of choking or getting sick at all. 

It's really just... I just don't feel the urge to eat, I guess. I just kind of forget. I wish I could give you a more helpful answer, I really do. Am I giving you the information you need so far? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight because you have not been eating?

Um, well, I guess that's sort of what brought me in, like I mentioned earlier. I hope you don't mind me repeating myself... but yeah, my eating has just gotten so off lately. Like I was saying, just managing a coffee and a granola bar before a shift is about all I can do some days. 

And because of that, I definitely have lost some weight. My scrubs are hanging really loose on me now, even though I'm absolutely not trying to lose anything. I haven't actually stepped on a scale to get an exact number for you, I'm so sorry about that. But... do you think the clothes fitting so differently means it's a significant amount? I hope that's helpful, I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly.
Has a doctor identified a medical condition that could be causing your reduced appetite?

Um, no, no doctor has mentioned anything like that to me. I haven't really been to see my regular doctor lately, to be honest. I hope that's okay, I know I probably should have gone in to get checked out. 

But as far as I know, there's no medical reason for it. I'm generally pretty healthy, physically, I mean. At least, I try to be. I really hope I'm not missing something important that I should be telling you. Does that answer your question alright?
How long has your reduced appetite and limited eating been going on?

Well, I guess the eating issues kind of tie into everything else. The steady, you know, just feeling really down and the loss of interest in everything... that settled in a bit later on, and it has been with me for roughly the past year and four months. So the appetite stuff has been happening for about that long, too. 

I try my best to push through it and keep up with my shifts, I really do. But it's been about a year and four months of just not having the drive for food or much else. I hope that's the kind of timeline you were asking for? I'm sorry if it's a bit vague, I didn't write down an exact date, but I just want to make sure I'm giving you a good enough answer.
When you are not feeling down or losing interest in things, does your lack of appetite and limited eating still happen?

Um, well... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I mean, the feeling down and the eating issues kind of all blend together for me, so it's hard to separate them out. I haven't really noticed if the appetite stuff happens when I'm feeling okay... mostly because I just haven't been feeling okay for a while now. 

I'm so sorry, I wish I had a clearer answer for you. I try to pay attention to these things, but it all just gets a bit muddled. Is it okay that I don't know for sure? I hope I'm not making your job harder by not having a better answer.
Did your reduced appetite begin before your low mood, after it, or around the same time?

Um, I think they started around the same time. It's just... well, what actually made me realize I needed to come in was that my eating has gotten so off track. I mean, some days I barely manage to get down a coffee and a granola bar before a shift at the hospital. 

I don't want you to think I'm neglecting myself on purpose, I'm really not. But I've noticed my scrubs have been hanging pretty loose lately, and I'm definitely not trying to lose weight or anything like that. I try to make sure I have enough energy for my patients, I really do. Is that the kind of information you needed? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
On days when your mood feels normal, do you still have very little interest in eating?

Well, like I was saying, it's just really hard to say because I haven't had many normal days lately. But... I mean, the whole reason I finally made the appointment is because the eating thing has just gotten so out of hand. I really try to eat, I promise I do, but some days it's just... maybe a coffee and a granola bar before I head to the hospital, and that's it. 

I don't want you to think I'm doing it on purpose, or that I have an eating disorder or something. I'm really not trying to lose weight at all. It's just... I noticed my scrubs are hanging pretty loose on me these days, and I know I need to be strong enough to do my job right. I hope it's okay that I brought that up again? I just want to make sure you understand how much I'm trying to keep things together.
Have there been any periods when your mood felt normal but you still had very little interest in eating?

I know you've asked about the normal days a few times now, and I really wish I could give you a better answer... I just, I really haven't had a normal mood in so long. But the reason I keep bringing up the eating—and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture—is that it's what finally pushed me to come see you. 

It's just gotten so off. Like I mentioned, there are days I can barely force down a coffee and a granola bar before I start my shift at the hospital. And I really don't want you to think I'm doing this to myself on purpose, because I know how important it is to stay healthy for my patients. But I can't help but notice my scrubs are hanging so loose on me lately. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight... it's just happening. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need to help me.
Have you needed nutritional supplements because of your limited eating?

No, no, I haven't needed any supplements or anything like that. I really try to manage it on my own, you know? I don't want to be a bother or need extra things. It's just... well, like I said, it's what brought me in, because my eating is just so off right now. 

I'm really trying, but some days it's just that coffee and granola bar before my shift, and I know that's not enough. And, um, seeing my scrubs hang so loose on me... it worries me, because I'm honestly not trying to lose weight. I want to be healthy. I hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, I just... I want you to know I'm not doing this on purpose. Is that okay? Did that answer your question about the supplements?
Have you been feeling tired or lacking energy nearly every day?

Well, I mean... I do feel pretty tired, yes. But I don't want to sound like I'm complaining about my job or anything, because I really do love what I do at the hospital. It's just... lately, even after I spend a full night in bed, my body feels like I just finished a double shift, you know? 

And it's a little embarrassing to admit, but by lunchtime I'm really fighting just to keep my thoughts together. I try to hide it from my coworkers, I promise I do, because I want to be a good team player. I'm still getting my work done, I just... it takes a lot more out of me than it used to. Is it normal to feel that drained? I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should be.
About how much weight have you lost since your appetite decreased?

Oh, gosh, I haven't actually stepped on a scale, so I don't have an exact number for you. I hope that's alright, I should have checked before coming in. I just know it's enough that my scrubs are really hanging off me lately. 

I'd guess maybe a size or two down? Like I said, I'm really not trying to lose any weight, I promise. It's just that my eating has been so off, with just the coffee and granola bar on some days, that it's just sort of falling off me. I know I need to do better, and I really am trying to force myself to eat more so I can be at my best for work. I hope that gives you a rough idea, even without the exact pounds?
When you are not feeling especially sad or tired, do you still find food itself uninteresting and have little desire to eat?

Well, um... I guess even on my better days, when I'm not feeling so down or exhausted, I still don't really have much of an appetite. I mean, I try, I really do. But food just doesn't seem... appealing, I guess? 

Like I mentioned earlier—and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I know that's what brought me in—my eating is just so off right now. Even when I'm feeling okay, I still struggle to get down more than that coffee and granola bar before a shift. And I know it's not good because, like I said, my scrubs are hanging loose and I'm really, honestly not trying to lose weight. I want to be healthy and do a good job at work. I just... I don't know why I don't want to eat. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions nearly every day?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I have trouble, exactly. I mean, I still get my work done at the hospital, and I make sure all my patients have what they need. I'm really careful about that, I promise. 

I guess... maybe I'm a little slower at figuring things out than I used to be? Like, sometimes I have to read a chart twice just to make sure I got it right, or I'll stand in the supply closet for a minute trying to remember what I went in there for. But I always figure it out! I don't want you to think I'm doing a bad job or making mistakes with patient care. I just... I guess my brain feels a little foggy sometimes, probably just because I'm so tired, right? I hope that's a normal thing to experience.
Have you been sleeping differently than usual since you began feeling depressed?

Well, I mean... I am still getting some sleep, so I don't want to make it sound like I'm completely falling apart or anything. I'm definitely still functioning for my shifts. 

It's just, um, maybe not the best quality sleep lately? I guess my sleep is a bit broken up. I'll lie there at night and just kind of replay everything from work in my head, making sure I didn't miss anything, and I find myself sort of listening for noises in the house. And then, usually, I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't seem to settle back down before my alarm goes off. 

But I'm sure that's just stress, right? I mean, everyone has trouble sleeping sometimes. I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should. Is it okay that I'm waking up that early, or is that something I should be worried about?
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of harming yourself?

Oh, no, please don't think that. I want to be really clear—I haven't made any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I promise. I know how important my job is, and I would never actually do something to harm myself. 

But, um... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... sometimes I do catch myself just kind of wishing I wouldn't wake up in the morning. Or just thinking it would be easier if I... disappeared, maybe? Just so I wouldn't have to feel so heavy and tired all the time. 

I hope that doesn't sound too terrible. I'm not a danger to myself or anyone else, I swear. It's probably just the exhaustion talking, right? I mean, it's normal to feel a little overwhelmed and think things like that when you're not sleeping well, isn't it? I really hope you don't think worse of me for saying that.
When your mood is back to normal, does your appetite remain low?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. When I'm feeling more like myself, my appetite is usually pretty normal, I think. I mean, I eat enough to keep my energy up for my shifts, and I definitely enjoy a good meal when I'm not feeling so down. 

I really try to take care of myself and eat right when I can. It's just lately, with everything feeling so heavy, I haven't been as hungry. But it definitely gets better when my mood lifts. That's a good sign, right? I hope that means I'm not doing too badly overall.
